reviewed_topics.topic: steering lock and KESSY-related steering-lock states
findings: Red flashing steering-wheel/exclamation: steering-lock fault; stop the vehicle and seek a specialist workshop. After switching the ignition off it may no longer be possible to switch the ignition on, lock the steering or operate electrical consumers.
Amber flashing steering-wheel/exclamation with a fault message: cautious continued driving is permitted; seek a specialist workshop.

Amber flashing steering-wheel/exclamation with a request to move the steering wheel: the steering lock has not released; move the wheel alternately in both directions, then stop and seek assistance if it remains locked.
Left and right green arrows are separate states.
A faster flashing rate identifies a fault on the corresponding side; the trailer indicator is a separate state.
The neutral A/main-beam symbol means the assistant is enabled.
The blue A/main-beam symbol means the assistant has automatically switched on main beam.
The driver must switch main beam manually when required; the camera-based system has stated detection limits.
The neutral A/main-beam symbol means Dynamic Light Assist is enabled.
The blue A/main-beam symbol means main beam is on; Dynamic Light Assist additionally adapts the beam pattern.
This equipment-specific state is not assigned to every Enyaq.
ACC activated is distinct from ACC currently regulating.
ACC deactivated, insufficient braking and predictive regulation states are separate indications.
Green means active and ready to intervene; amber means the system is intervening in steering.
Automatic activation and a system-unavailable message are described separately.
Active with speed and adaptive lane guidance, speed-only regulation, and lane-guidance-only are separate composite states.
White and red steering take-over requests have different urgency.
Displayed road signs are informational; actual roadside signs take precedence.
The display varies with the detected sign, supplementary sign, country units and trailer connection.
A cup symbol accompanies a break recommendation based on evaluated vehicle control.
The system does not warn when the driver falls into microsleep; operating range is 60–200 km/h.
Reset conditions are ignition off, driver belt/door sequence, or a stop longer than 15 minutes.
